name: LITEON
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: LITEON is the #2 supplier in AI server power (~30% share versus Delta's 60%+ per brokerage estimates) with the sector's strongest position in battery backup units — 2025 BBU shipments ran roughly 30x the prior year, and BBUs turn from optional (GB200) to standard (GB300/Rubin) — and Q2 2026 delivered an all-time record: EPS NT$3.14 (+126%), record gross margin 27.2%, with AI products expected to exceed 30% of 2026 revenue. BACKGROUND: Founded 1975, the first electronics company listed on the Taiwan exchange; chairman Tom Soong, president Anson Chiu ('no longer an ODM/OEM — a solution provider'); three segments with Cloud & AIoT now 54% of sales (from 32% in 2022). A member of NVIDIA's 800 VDC power-components tier alongside Delta, Megmeet, Flex, and BizLink. Committed US$919M to a McKinney, Texas plant for HVDC power racks; 2026 capex raised to NT$18B; non-China capacity heading to 70% by 2027.
ecosystemRole: We assess LITEON as the leading second source in NVIDIA-class rack power and the direct competitive triangulation point for Megmeet — the three names share the power-components tier, and the sidecar power-rack fight among them decides who captures the fastest-growing hardware segment in the AIDC chain. Basis: NVIDIA's own 800V partner roster; KGI-attributed platform data placing LITEON as the lead second source (strongest at a US CSP with an aggressive ASIC timeline); and Chinese-press reporting that Megmeet displaced LITEON at #2 on NVL72 power shelves — contested, high-stakes, and unresolved. LITEON's differentiated asset is the BBU franchise (investing since 2010, first large cloud adoption 2017) plus PSU-BBU firmware co-design; its 800V power rack reaches mass production Q1 2027, about a step behind Delta, with ASIC customers first and GPU clients potentially Q2 2027.

productsAndServices.name: AI rack power (power shelves, PSUs, 800 VDC Power Rack)
productsAndServices.description: Shipping: 33 kW power shelves, 5.5 kW PSUs, 8.5 kW PSU+BBU pairs (volume production), 110 kW power shelves for NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 (three-phase input, intelligent load balancing, transient-surge handling; 18.3 kW PSUs), and an 800 VDC 660 kW power rack — scaling to >1.5 MW racks in 2H 2026 with a 2.5 kW 50V→12V DC-DC brick. PSU/shelf specs: >100 W/in³ power density, >97.5% efficiency, 40-70°C operating range.
productsAndServices.positioning: Lead second source behind Delta; the liquid-cooled 800 VDC rack debuted at Computex 2026. Mass production Q1 2027 after a 13-week qualification from August 2026 sampling — ASIC customers onboard first.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: B2B direct to hyperscalers/CSPs/ODMs (CIPS business group); QCT joint Vera Rubin demo at GTC 2026.
targetSegments: Hyperscaler custom-ASIC programs (two new North American CSPs entered the approved-vendor list this year)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Management targets US$1B revenue per key account within two years; Texas plant localizes HVDC power-rack output for North America.

productsAndServices.name: Battery backup units & supercapacitor shelves (the BBU franchise)
productsAndServices.description: Rack-level DC-coupled BBUs replacing centralized UPS: 12 kW/2U 50V BBU shelf (45 s full-power backup), 22 kW/3U 800V supercapacitor shelf (60 s), designs targeting 2-minute ride-through (keeping CDU coolant flowing — 'power resilience firewall'); ~5x power density versus five years ago; microsecond 'Always Backup' switching via PSU-BBU firmware integration (LITEON builds both sides); UL 9540A-type fire validation; backup ratios configurable above 1:0.7.
productsAndServices.positioning: LITEON's clearest lead: investing since 2010, first large cloud adoption 2017, 2025 shipments ~30x prior year — and the architecture shift makes BBUs standard equipment on GB300/Rubin racks. BBU is ~20-25% of the cloud segment and has been capacity-constrained.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct CSP deployments with long-term B2B history.
productsAndServices.roadmap: The GB300 NVL72 collaboration with NVIDIA (energy storage + power capping + GPU load management) cut grid peak load ~30% — the productized version of the power-smoothing problem.

productsAndServices.name: Liquid cooling (CDUs, cold plates, sidecars)
productsAndServices.description: 2.1 MW in-row CDU, 280 kW and 120 kW in-rack CDUs, 140 kW liquid-to-air sidecar, 600 kW in-row L2L, GB300 NVL72 cold plates, fanless 5,600 W cold-plate titanium PSU; MGX and ORV3 racks rated beyond 3,000 kg with <2 mm tolerance.
productsAndServices.positioning: A credible fast-follower thermal line that lets LITEON quote power+cooling rack integration — the same bundling logic as Delta, a tier smaller.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Same CIPS rack-integration channel (assembly 'up to level 9').
productsAndServices.roadmap: Liquid-cooled 800 VDC rack (cold-plate cooled power components) debuted June 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Legacy & diversification (opto, IT/consumer, LEO power, optics bet)
productsAndServices.description: Optoelectronics (16% of 1H26 sales): opto-semis, automotive lighting, IR sensing. IT & Consumer (30%): PC/gaming power, adapters — guided softer in H2. Growth options: LEO satellite user-terminal power (guided to multiple-fold growth), 5G/AI-RAN (MWC 2026, U-MEDIA tender), and a US$34.3M / ~21% stake in Singapore InP laser IDM DenseLight for rack-scale optical interconnect (no material revenue before late 2027).
productsAndServices.positioning: The legacy mix funds the pivot; DenseLight is the CPO-era optionality play against a cited US$35B optical-interconnect TAM by 2030.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Segment mix continues shifting toward Cloud & AIoT (54% and rising).

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess the BBU franchise is LITEON's structural edge and the architecture shift amplifies it. Basis: BBUs move from optional (GB200) to standard (GB300/Rubin); 2025 BBU shipments ~30x prior year against acknowledged capacity constraints; and the 800V power rack embeds BBU and supercap shelves — LITEON's strongest products become non-discretionary content.

(High confidence) We assess LITEON is a step behind Delta on the 800V GPU-side ramp and is routing around it via ASIC customers. Basis: its own disclosed timeline (sampling August 2026 → mass production Q1 2027, ASIC first, GPU clients 'potentially Q2 2027') versus Delta demoing at GTC with an NVIDIA DC-DC exclusive; KGI-attributed data has LITEON strongest at a US CSP with an aggressive ASIC deployment timeline.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the Megmeet threat is real but not yet resolved against LITEON. Basis: Chinese-press reports of Megmeet displacing LITEON at #2 on NVL72 shelves conflict with LITEON's record shipments and AVL additions (two new North American CSPs this year); both can be true if the market is growing faster than share shifts — but the sidecar power-rack segment LITEON is tooling Texas for is the same one Megmeet claims first-mover position in, and independent analysis projects that TAM peaking around 2028.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the balance sheet is carrying the ramp visibly. Basis: short-term loans +132% to NT$31.4B, inventory +25%, cash-conversion cycle out 17 days to 64, net cash down NT$11.8B — plus a 200M-share GDR/placement authorization; customer-subsidized component stockpiling mitigates but does not remove the working-capital strain.

(Low confidence) We assess consensus sees the stock near fully valued into the ramp. Basis: price target ~NT$253.5 versus ~NT$247 (~2.6% upside) at ~20.5x forward earnings — a sharp contrast with Delta's wide bull-bear spread; the market is paying for execution already promised. Pre-2026 the company missed estimates four times across the trailing window — the AI narrative only overwhelmed the miss pattern from Q2 2026.
